subject: physics_2
question_text: What is the value of neutron multiplication factor in a controlled chain reaction and in an uncontrolled chain reaction?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. PRINTED ERROR CORRECTED. The book (p.49) prints both lines with the word "controlled": "In controlled chain reaction, the value of multiplication factor K = 1. In controlled chain reaction, K > 1." The second line must read UNCONTROLLED — K > 1 is the runaway case. Controlled: K = 1, the neutron population stays steady, as in a reactor. Uncontrolled: K > 1, each generation is larger than the last, as in an atom bomb. Hand-checked against the definition K = (neutrons in the present generation)/(neutrons in the previous generation), which the book itself prints correctly in SAQ 5.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Controlled: K = 1
lines: The neutron multiplication factor K is the
number of neutrons in one generation divided
by the number in the previous generation.
The number of fissions per second stays
steady, as in a nuclear reactor.
steps.margin_note: First mark. K = 1 and the word steady.
steps.why: K = 1 means every fission produces exactly one further fission, so the reaction neither grows nor dies away. Control rods are moved to hold K at this value.
common_mistakes: Writing K < 1 for a reactor. K < 1 means the reaction stops.
Giving the value with no reason. Say that the rate stays steady.

recall.must_convey: That in a controlled chain reaction the multiplication factor K equals 1 and the rate of fission stays steady, as in a reactor.

steps.memory_tip: One fission hands on exactly one — K = 1 keeps a reactor level.

steps.label: Uncontrolled: K > 1
lines: Each generation has more neutrons than the
one before, so the number of fissions grows
very fast, as in an atom bomb.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. K > 1 belongs to the UNCONTROLLED reaction.
steps.why: The book prints this second line as "In controlled chain reaction, K > 1", repeating the word controlled. That is a printing slip: K > 1 makes the neutron number grow in geometric progression, which is the uncontrolled case. A controlled reaction is exactly the one held at K = 1.
common_mistakes: Copying the book and writing "controlled" on both lines. The second is uncontrolled.
Writing K = 0 for uncontrolled. The value is greater than 1.

recall.must_convey: That in an uncontrolled chain reaction the multiplication factor K is greater than 1, so the number of fissions grows rapidly, as in an atom bomb.
accept: uncontrolled reaction K is more than one

steps.memory_tip: Reactor holds K at 1; a bomb lets K go above 1.

insider_note: Write both values with the word controlled or uncontrolled beside each. The printed book repeats "controlled" on both lines; copying that costs the second mark.
